learn: Undefined terms in geometry are point, line and plane.
A segment has two endpoints; a ray has one endpoint and extends forever; collinear points lie on one line.
Postulates are accepted statements; theorems are proved.

learn: Inductive reasoning finds patterns and makes conjectures.
Deductive reasoning uses facts, definitions and logic to reach certain conclusions.
A counterexample disproves a conjecture.

lessons.try: Make a conjecture from a pattern and test it.

learn: A conditional is "if p, then q".
Converse: if q, then p. Inverse: if not p, then not q. Contrapositive: if not q, then not p.
A conditional and its contrapositive are logically equivalent.

learn: Complementary angles sum to 90°; supplementary to 180°.
Vertical angles are congruent; a linear pair is supplementary.
Angle bisectors divide an angle into two congruent angles.
lessons.try: Find unknown angles in a diagram of intersecting lines.

learn: Corresponding, alternate interior and alternate exterior angles are congruent when lines are parallel.
Same-side interior angles are supplementary.
The converses prove that lines are parallel.

learn: Parallel lines have equal slopes; perpendicular lines have slopes whose product is -1.
Find the equation of a parallel or perpendicular line through a point.
Distance formula: d = √((x₂ - x₁)² + (y₂ - y₁)²).

learn: Translations, reflections and rotations preserve size and shape (isometries).
Translation (x, y) → (x + a, y + b).
Reflection over the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, -y); over y = x: (x, y) → (y, x).
lessons.try: Translate, reflect and rotate a triangle on a coordinate grid.

learn: Rotate 90° counterclockwise about the origin: (x, y) → (-y, x).
Rotational symmetry: a figure maps onto itself after a rotation less than 360°.

lessons.try: Rotate a figure 90° and 180° about the origin.

learn: A dilation with scale factor k from the origin: (x, y) → (kx, ky).
k > 1 enlarges; 0 < k < 1 reduces. Dilations create similar figures.
A composition applies one transformation after another.
lessons.try: Dilate a figure by 2, then translate it.

learn: Triangles are congruent by SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS or HL (right triangles).
SSA and AAA do not guarantee congruence.
CPCTC: corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent.
lessons.try: Identify which criterion proves pairs of triangles congruent.

learn: A proof lists statements and reasons in logical order.
Reasons include given information, definitions, postulates and theorems.
Start with what is given and end with what you want to prove.
lessons.try: Write a two-column proof that base angles of an isosceles triangle are congruent.

learn: The base angles of an isosceles triangle are congruent.
An equilateral triangle is also equiangular: each angle is 60°.
The converse also holds: if two angles are congruent, the opposite sides are congruent.

learn: Interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°.
An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.
The triangle inequality: the sum of any two sides exceeds the third.
check: Remote interior angles 50° and 65° give exterior angle...
lessons.try: Test whether sides 5, 7 and 13 form a triangle.

learn: Medians meet at the centroid, which divides each median 2:1.
Perpendicular bisectors meet at the circumcentre; angle bisectors at the incentre; altitudes at the orthocentre.
The midsegment is parallel to the third side and half its length.
check: A midsegment is ___ the third side's length.
lessons.try: Construct the centroid of a triangle with paper folding.

learn: The longest side is opposite the largest angle.
The hinge theorem compares triangles with two congruent sides.
Use these to order sides and angles.

learn: Similar figures have congruent corresponding angles and proportional sides.
The scale factor is the ratio of corresponding sides.
Perimeters scale by k; areas by k²; volumes by k³.

If the scale factor is 2, volume scales by...

learn: Triangles are similar by AA, SAS~ or SSS~.
Shadows and mirrors use similar triangles to measure tall objects.
A 2 m person casting a 3 m shadow next to a tree casting a 12 m shadow means the tree is 8 m tall.

learn: The triangle proportionality theorem: a line parallel to one side divides the other two sides proportionally.
The angle bisector theorem divides the opposite side in the ratio of the adjacent sides.
Set up and solve proportions.

learn: a² + b² = c² in right triangles.
Converse: if a² + b² = c², the triangle is right; if a² + b² > c², acute; if less, obtuse.
Pythagorean triples: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17.

30-60-90: short leg x, long leg x√3, hypotenuse 2x.

learn: SOH-CAH-TOA: sin = opposite/hypotenuse; cos = adjacent/hypotenuse; tan = opposite/adjacent.
Use inverse functions to find angles: θ = tan⁻¹(opp/adj).
Angles of elevation and depression model real problems.

learn: Interior angle sum = (n - 2) × 180°.
Each interior angle of a regular n-gon = (n - 2) × 180° ÷ n.
Exterior angles of any convex polygon sum to 360°.

learn: Opposite sides are parallel and congruent; opposite angles are congruent; diagonals bisect each other.
Rectangles have congruent diagonals; rhombuses have perpendicular diagonals; squares have both.
Use these properties to prove a quadrilateral is a parallelogram.

learn: A trapezoid has exactly one pair of parallel sides (bases).
The midsegment of a trapezoid = (b₁ + b₂) ÷ 2.
Kites have two pairs of adjacent congruent sides and perpendicular diagonals.
